skill.name: gjalla-breakdown
skill.description: Break a feature spec into intentional waves and bite-sized tasks grouped by dependency. Use after a spec is written to prepare for easy-to-track implementation.
skill.summary: Turn feature specifications into dependency-ordered waves of small, verifiable implementation tasks.
skill.author: gjalla

security_audit.summary: The single static finding is a false positive. SKILL.md contains planning guidance only, with no system reconnaissance, executable code, external commands, or prompt injection.

static_findings.snippet: To avoid overload, try to keep the total task count under 20 for a single spec; split larger feature

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 29 only recommends limiting task counts and splitting large features. It performs no system reconnaissance and requests no system information.

content.value_statement: Large feature specifications can be difficult to sequence and track. This skill creates dependency-ordered waves of small tasks with files and acceptance checks.
actual_capabilities: Extracts behavioral requirements and technical changes from a feature specification.
Divides implementation work into small tasks that target one or two files.
Maps dependencies between tasks before assigning implementation order.
Groups independent tasks into parallel waves and dependent tasks into sequential waves.
Adds exact file paths, task dependencies, acceptance checks, and completion markers.
Includes documentation, testing, and verification work in the breakdown.
limitations: Requires a sufficiently detailed feature specification or agent plan.
Does not implement tasks, modify files, or run verification commands.
Cannot guarantee file paths without accurate repository context.
Large features may require multiple specifications to remain under 20 tasks.

use_cases.title: Plan a Feature Implementation
use_cases.description: Convert an approved specification into sequenced tasks that are easy to assign, implement, and verify.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Parallel Work
use_cases.description: Identify independent tasks that multiple contributors can complete during the same implementation wave.

use_cases.title: Prepare Agent Execution
use_cases.description: Create a structured implementation plan with clear files, dependencies, and acceptance checks for coding agents.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Breakdown
prompt_templates.prompt: Break this feature specification into dependency-ordered waves. Give each task an ID, description, files, dependencies, and acceptance check: [specification]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a complete feature specification is ready for implementation planning.

prompt_templates.title: Plan With Repository Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this specification and repository context. Produce implementation waves with tasks touching one or two files each: [specification and repository context]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when known modules and file paths should guide task boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Parallel Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Break down this specification for parallel delivery. Minimize dependencies within each wave and include tests, documentation, and verification: [specification]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when several contributors can work simultaneously.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve a Complex Dependency Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a wave plan for this complex feature. Explain dependencies, flag uncertain file ownership, and split the work if it exceeds 20 tasks: [specification]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for large cross-module features that may require multiple specifications.

output_examples.input: Add email verification to account registration.
output: Wave 1: Add verification fields and migration, with schema checks as acceptance criteria.
Wave 2: Create token generation and delivery tasks that depend on the schema update.
Wave 3: Add verification endpoints, user interface changes, tests, and documentation.

output_examples.input: Add saved dashboard filters for signed-in users.
output: W1-T1: Define stored filter data and persistence behavior.
W2-T1: Add service operations after the data model is available.
W2-T2: Build interface controls in parallel with service integration tests.
W3-T1: Complete end-to-end verification and documentation.

best_practices: Provide the approved specification and relevant repository context before requesting a breakdown.
Keep each task small enough to produce a focused, reviewable change.
Review file paths, dependencies, and acceptance checks before implementation begins.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague requirements that omit expected behavior or technical constraints.
Do not combine unrelated modules into one large task without a clear dependency reason.
Do not treat tasks within one wave as parallel when they depend on each other.

faq.question: What input does this skill need?
faq.answer: Provide a written feature specification or agent plan with behavioral requirements and expected technical changes.

faq.question: What does each task include?
faq.answer: Each task includes an ID, description, exact file paths, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and a completion marker.

faq.question: How are waves ordered?
faq.answer: Waves are sequential. Tasks within one wave should be independent and suitable for parallel work.

faq.question: Does the skill implement the plan?
faq.answer: No. It creates the breakdown but does not edit files, run commands, or complete tasks.

faq.question: How large should a breakdown be?
faq.answer: The guidance recommends fewer than 20 tasks. Split larger features into multiple specifications.

faq.question: Does the breakdown include testing and documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill explicitly includes tests, verification, documentation, and other completion work.
